- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is rising, model often over-optimistically peaks; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply 1–3% downward correction in next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model tends to lag; add 1–2% upward bias for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often under-reacts; increase forecast sensitivity by 1–2% for next 7 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by >2% over 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias of 1–3% for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after spike, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
